body.statement: There exist constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\), depending only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), such that for every \(n\ge2\), \[c\rho_n\le R_n\le C\rho_n,\qquad \rho_n=n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}.\] The upper bound is attained by \(\widehat\tau_n(0)\), and the lower bound is over the same singleton exact-uniform, bounded-overlap, Bernoulli class through genuine fixed-\(n\) product laws. The theorem establishes that the nuisance-dominated candidate from KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE persists in this exact-uniform boundary experiment, which is not covered by its perforated-support lower witness.
body.justification: The theorem determines the exact-uniform minimax order and closes the specific support gap left by the published lower experiment.
body.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE proves the candidate exponent on a density-qualified model whose displayed hard laws have perforated local support; it does not prove this lower bound after fixing \(P_X\) to exact uniformity.
body.consumer: The result tells users whether learning rough propensity and outcome regressions imposes an unavoidable pointwise CATE penalty even under a benign known design.
